newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Canal overhaul partially completed.
newsitem.headline: Panama Canal overhaul partially completed.

text.p: The Panama Canal Commission (PCC) said Wednesday that both lanes of traffic at the Gatun locks were scheduled to start operating that evening.

Traffic at the Gatun locks were scheduled to restart at 6 p.m. local time/2400 GMT "marking the end of a 10-day scheduled outage in one lane for locks maintenance and improvements", the PCC said in a statement.
The PCC said the Canal would continue to operate at its highest capacity, with 24-hour relay operations scheduled in one lane, with regular lockages planned for the other for the next three days.
Relay operations maximize the number of ships that can pass through one lane of traffic at the locks.
Overhaul work continued on the Miraflores locks' west lane at the Pacific entrance to the Canal, with 24-hour relay operations in effect for the open lane.

Canal track personnel are carrying out low track rehabilitation, miter gate overhaul and other inspections, cleaning and repair projects during the planned, 13-day outage, which is scheduled to end just before midnight on July 19.
Morning and evening relay operations are scheduled to begin in both Miraflores lanes July 20, the PCC said.

A total of 23 vessels transited the waterway on Tuesday, with 31 scheduled for Wednesday. "Just after midnight today, July 16, 67 ships were awaiting transit of the waterway, with 11 of those not ready for scheduling," the PCC said.
The PCC said 40 ships were expected to arrive at the Canal on Wednesday, with 37 arrivals expected for Thursday.
Average Canal Waters Time (CWT) -- the period that a vessel spends between its arrival and completed transit of the waterway -- was 37.4 hours on July 15.
"The Panama Canal Commission will continue to use all available resources to keep any transit delays to a minimum during the locks overhaul," the PCC said.
(( -- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507 223 7739))
